title: The canonical maps of formal glueing: localized S-module structure, swap of two localizations, localization of a base change
statement:
Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $P$ be an $R$-module and $f,g\in R$. For an $R$-module $Q$ and $e\in R$ let $Q_e$ be the localization of $Q$ at $e$ with its localization map $Q\to Q_e$, $q\mapsto q/1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], and for an $R$-linear map $h:Q\to Q'$ let $h_e:Q_e\to Q'_e$, $q/e^n\mapsto h(q)/e^n$, be its localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; $Q\otimes_RS$ and $h\otimes_RS$ are the base changes [def-weil-module-base-change], and an $S$-module is regarded as an $R$-module through $\varphi$.
(1) For $R$-linear maps $k:Q\to Q'$, $h:Q'\to Q''$ and $h':Q'\to Q''$ one has $(h\circ k)_e=h_e\circ k_e$, $(h+h')_e=h_e+h'_e$ and $(\mathrm{id}_Q)_e=\mathrm{id}_{Q_e}$. Consequently, if $Q$ is an $S$-module, the maps $(s\cdot)_e:Q_e\to Q_e$, $s\in S$ (the localizations of the multiplications $q\mapsto sq$), make $Q_e$ an $S$-module, i.e. $s\cdot(q/e^n)=(sq)/e^n$, whose underlying $R$-module structure is the given one; the localization map $Q\to Q_e$ is $S$-linear; and $h_e$ is $S$-linear whenever $h:Q\to Q'$ is an $S$-linear map of $S$-modules.
(2) The elements $f$ and $g$ act bijectively on the $R$-module $(P_g)_f$, and there is exactly one $R$-linear map $\sigma^P_{f,g}:(P_f)_g\to(P_g)_f$ with $\sigma^P_{f,g}((p/1)/1)=(p/1)/1$ for all $p\in P$. It is given by $\sigma^P_{f,g}((p/f^a)/g^b)=(p/g^b)/f^a$ ($p\in P$, $a,b\ge0$), and it is an isomorphism with inverse $\sigma^P_{g,f}$.
(3) The element $f$ acts bijectively on $P_f\otimes_RS$, and there is exactly one $R$-linear map $c^P_f:(P\otimes_RS)_f\to P_f\otimes_RS$ with $c^P_f((p\otimes s)/1)=(p/1)\otimes s$ for all $p\in P$, $s\in S$. It is given by $c^P_f((p\otimes s)/f^e)=(p/f^e)\otimes s$, it is $S$-linear for the $S$-module structure of (1) on $(P\otimes_RS)_f$, and it is an isomorphism of $S$-modules.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark 05EL (label remark-glueing-data, line 24641): the 'canonical isomorphisms' can_i : (M ⊗_R S)_{f_i} → M_{f_i} ⊗_R S and can_ij : (M_{f_i})_{f_j} → (M_{f_j})_{f_i} of the functor Can, used implicitly in conditions (a), (b) of the objects; existence and uniqueness from Algebra Lemma 07K0 (algebra.tex line 1171, label lemma-universal-property-localization-module); (P ⊗_R S)_f ≅ P_f ⊗_R S from Algebra Lemma 00DK (line 2088, label lemma-tensor-localization)

mathlib_searches.query: localization of base change of a module is base change of localization, (M ⊗ S)_f ≅ M_f ⊗ S
mathlib_searches.results: IsLocalizedModule.rTensor (Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.BaseChange:244), IsLocalization.Away.tensorEquiv, IsLocalization.tensor, isLocalizedModule_iff_isBaseChange, IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange, IsLocalization.algebraTensorEquiv
mathlib_searches.verdict: candidate for the R-linear part of clause (3): IsLocalizedModule.rTensor (BaseChange.lean:244-252) says that for a localization map g : M → M' at a submonoid, AlgebraTensorModule.rTensor R N g is again a localization map; with g = P → P_f and N = S it makes P ⊗_R S → P_f ⊗_R S a localization at the powers of f, and IsLocalizedModule.iso/linearEquiv then gives an R-linear isomorphism (P ⊗_R S)_f ≅ P_f ⊗_R S. The S-linearity and clauses (1), (2) are not covered; not a leaf

note: Claim moved out of def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data (well-definedness of its data: the S-module structure of P_f, the maps sigma^P_{f,g} and c^P_f). The definition names it in `pointers`, not in stmt_deps (a definition does not cite a lemma about its own data).
